subject: The family recipes that never made it into a cookbook
html:
Hi Felicity,

I hope you’re having a lovely week. I’m Chaten, and I wanted to introduce you to two communities I’ve been building around something very simple: the food and drinks that keep us connected to people.

I thought the question of how we preserve everyday family recipes, including the small details that never make it into a cookbook, might be of interest for a food feature.

Other People’s Recipes began with an idea I wrote down in 2000: to give family recipes, and the memories that belong to them, a place to live on. A handwritten recipe tucked inside a cookbook, a dish someone always brings to the table, or the meal you wish you’d asked a loved one to teach you.

Today, OPR is a living cookbook where people share their recipes in their own names, alongside the stories behind them. One lovely example is Gautam, who turned to his mum, Shobha, for a recipe as he prepared to open his first restaurant. Her Tandoori Aloo Nazakat now has a home in the cookbook, with their story beside it.

Its sister community, Other People’s Cocktails, brings that same warmth to the glass: the drink a friend introduced you to, a holiday discovery, or an alcohol-free favourite that has become part of a family celebration. We’d love people to share the memory as well as the recipe.

With Christmas approaching, I wondered whether there might be a story here for your audience about the recipes and traditions we pass on, and the ones we risk losing if we never write them down. A simple invitation to save one family recipe could be a lovely place to start.

I’d be delighted to tell you more, share a few published stories, or help explore a feature or cooking item that would suit your audience. Any introductions to contributors would, of course, be with their permission.

You can have a look here:

Other People’s Recipes: https://otherpeoplesrecipes.co.uk/
Other People’s Cocktails: https://otherpeoplescocktails.co.uk/

Thank you for taking a moment to read this. If it feels like something your readers or viewers would enjoy, I’d love to have a chat.

Warm wishes,
Chaten
Founder, Other People’s Recipes & Other People’s Cocktails
chaten@otherpeoplesrecipes.co.uk
